This reads well. Everything is in order — checker, typecheck, lint, format, and 38 unit/integration tests all pass, and I confirmed against the live server that the 422 error shape and success shape match what the HTTP adapter expects.

Summary of what was added:

- **`services/orders.contract.ts`** / **`services/orders.http.ts`** — the `OrdersApi` interface and its HTTP adapter (`GET /api/customers`, `POST /api/orders`, with `OrderRejected` carrying the 422 field errors).
- **`modules/orders/`** — a full module (state/effects/view/index) following the project's existing pattern:
  - `orders.state.ts`: draft signals, field errors, a pure `validateOrder` (quantity 1–1000 whole number, note ≤200 chars, customer required) run *before* any request is sent.
  - `orders.effects.ts`: `resource()` (with retry/backoff) to load customers, `mutation()` (no key, so a form waits for its own submit rather than racing) to place the order, mapping `OrderRejected` to field errors and anything else to a general form error.
  - `orders.view.ts`: the form (`data-testid="order-form"`) with customer select, quantity, note, per-field error nodes (`error-customer`/`error-quantity`/`error-note`), a submit button (`data-testid="submit"`) disabled while pending, and a `data-testid="created"` message on success.
  - `orders.css`, wired into `styles/global.css`.
- **`app.ts`** now mounts both the orders and devices modules via `mount()`.
- Test coverage in `orders.state.test.ts` and `orders.effects.test.ts` (validation, submit lifecycle, 422 handling, generic failure, double-submit guard).

One caveat: no browser automation tool was available in this environment, so I verified the DOM/event wiring by reasoning through the runtime source (`instantiate.js`) rather than clicking through it live — but I did confirm the live server's actual 422/200 response shapes via curl match the adapter's assumptions, and the full architecture-checker/typecheck/lint/test suite is green.

reply.text:
It's done.

Root cause: the `<input min="1" max="1000">` relied on the browser's native constraint validation to block out-of-range submits. That silently intercepted the `submit` event before our own handler ever ran — so no server call happened, but our own `data-testid="error-quantity"` never rendered either, since the app's validation code was never reached. Fix: added `novalidate` to the `<form>` in `modules/orders/orders.view.ts` so the app's own `validateOrder` is always what runs and renders the error, with the browser never intercepting.

I also added `modules/orders/orders.view.test.ts`, which drives the real DOM (`select`/`input`/`button` elements and a genuine `submit` event) instead of calling `effects.submit()` directly — the existing test style bypassed the form entirely, which is exactly why this bug went undetected. It covers: out-of-range quantity, blank required fields, a valid submission reaching the server and clearing the form, and the submit button's disabled state during the request.

Full suite: architecture checker, typecheck, lint, format, and all 42 tests (including the new ones) pass clean.
